newsitem.title: USA: Ill. senate panel defeats education funding plan.
newsitem.headline: Ill. senate panel defeats education funding plan.

text.p: An Illinois Senate committee on Friday voted down Gov. Jim Edgar's proposed 25 percent income tax increase for education funding and property tax relief, a spokesman for the governor said.

The Senate revenue committee voted 6-4 to defeat the measure, which would raise the income tax rate from 3 percent to 3.75 percent to generate $600 million for schools and $900 million of property tax cuts, spokesman John Webber said.

Illinois representatives approved the plan Thursday 62-55 mostly along party lines in the Democrat-controlled House. The Republican-controlled Senate committee voted along party lines to defeat the plan and began considering financing alternatives, Webber said.

"The word we have got is they are trying to fly some dice in revenue and come up with some kind of alternative that we don't think is going to have enough votes to pass the Senate," Webber said. "The only plan that can pass today (Friday) if it is called on the full floor of the Senate is our plan. We have the 30 votes to do it."
Webber said that Republican Senate President James "Pate" Philip's opposition to the Republican governor's plan has stalled it at this point.
"It does not have to be dead, it can be reconsidered and should be," Webber said.
The Edgar plan also included capturing $100 million of new revenue growth to back up to $2 billion of bonds for a school construction matching program with local districts.
Sen. James Clayborne Jr., D-East St. Louis, sponsored the Edgar plan in the Senate.
